title: Falling Barometer Forecast Trainer
creator: Hank R. & Claude Code
subject: Environmental Monitoring
description: Six pressure traces, the last twelve hours hidden. Commit to a forecast, then find out. Several traces are built so that the value and the trend disagree.

learningObjectives: Predict approaching weather from a pressure trace.
Judge the rate of change rather than the absolute value.
Justify a prediction from the physical behaviour of rising and sinking air.
prerequisites: Chapter 7 sections on highs, lows and why air rises

keyQuestions: Which tells you more, the pressure or the change in pressure?
A reading of 1025 hPa is falling 4 hPa every three hours. What do you do?
What was the second needle on an old barometer for?
commonMisconceptions: Believing low pressure by itself means bad weather.
Believing high pressure by itself means safe weather.
Reading the daily two-hectopascal tide as an approaching system.
assessmentOpportunities: Predicts from the tendency rather than the absolute value.
Recognises the diurnal oscillation as non-weather.
Justifies a forecast by reference to a rate, in hPa per hour, and a physical mechanism.
